## Verdict (one line)
**Final vs Baseline blood shows the negligible effects** — it is the least-affected contrast under the mandated binomial exact test and under all six sensitivity variants, and its effects are noise-scale (median |log2FC| 0.216, only 4.8% of genes above |log2FC|>1, 133 genes significant *and* >4-fold, 189 contrast-exclusive DEGs) whereas both dentate-gyrus contrasts move about half the transcriptome (median |log2FC| 1.11/1.13, 53% above |log2FC|>1, ~8,700 genes >4-fold, and 91% Jaccard overlap with each other, i.e. one large shared tissue signature).

## 1. Primary test (headline: nominal p<0.05; all 90 libraries, all 25,402 genes, arms pooled, p0 = N_A/(N_A+N_B), two-sided `scipy.stats.binomtest` on rounded normalized counts)

| contrast (A vs B) | genes | tested | untestable (n=0) | p0 | **sig p<0.05** | % tested | ×chance | excess vs chance | FDR<0.05 | % | med\|log2FC\| | p95\|log2FC\| | frac\|log2FC\|>1 | median pooled depth/gene |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Final vs Baseline blood** | 25,402 | 22,060 | 3,342 | 0.5841 | **17,215** | **78.04%** | 15.6× | +16,112 | 17,046 | 77.27% | **0.2159** | **0.989** | **4.82%** | 2,668 |
| Dentate gyrus vs Baseline blood | 25,402 | 22,990 | 2,412 | 0.4936 | 20,135 | 87.58% | 17.5× | +19,036 | 20,109 | 87.47% | 1.1107 | 7.24 | 52.78% | 5,264 |
| Dentate gyrus vs Final blood | 25,402 | 22,861 | 2,541 | 0.4097 | 20,212 | 88.41% | 17.7× | +19,131 | 20,150 | 88.14% | 1.1269 | 7.36 | 53.19% | 5,496 |

(3,342 untestable vs the 2,210 all-zero genes: extra genes arise because per-arm sums <0.5 round to 0 — a rounding side-effect of the fixed protocol.)

## 2. Sensitivity columns (nominal p<0.05 counts; % of tested in parentheses)

| contrast | primary | V1 p0=0.5 | V2 paired sign (30 subj) | V3 outlier lib dropped | V4 expressed-only (≥1 both arms) | V5 median-of-ratios renormalised | V6 Welch t (replicate-aware, reference only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Final vs Baseline blood | 17,215 (78.0) | 14,859 (67.4) | 9,803 (44.4) | 17,215 (78.0) | 15,597 (91.8 of 16,982) | 17,200 (78.0) | 10,210 (46.3) |
| DG vs Baseline blood | 20,135 (87.6) | 20,041 (87.2) | 19,114 (83.0) | 20,191 (87.8) | 15,524 (95.9 of 16,187) | 20,126 (87.5) | 19,470 (84.6) |
| DG vs Final blood | 20,212 (88.4) | 20,007 (87.5) | 18,825 (82.2) | 20,276 (88.7) | 15,448 (96.0 of 16,089) | 20,208 (88.4) | 19,230 (84.0) |

**Ranking is identical in every variant: Final vs Baseline blood < DG vs Baseline ≈ DG vs Final.** Explicitly, as requested: dropping the Lars2-dominated `Control_dentate_gyrus5` library does *not* change the ranking (DG hit counts move +56/+64 genes, FvB unchanged because the sample is in the DG arm only, so its effect on the DG arm is via the null p0 and is negligible), and the expressed-genes-only restriction *increases* all hit rates but leaves the ordering unchanged (91.8% vs 95.9/96.0%). The size factors from median-of-ratios are 0.986–1.040, i.e. the supplied normalized counts are already properly normalized — the hit rates are not a normalization artifact.

## 3. Effect-size summaries and p-value distributions (primary)
- effect sizes: med signed log2FC = 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.0094 (no global shift in any contrast); med |log2FC| 0.216 vs 1.111 vs 1.127; p95 |log2FC| 0.99 vs 7.24 vs 7.36.
- significance **plus** a biological effect size (this is where the three contrasts separate by an order of magnitude):

| contrast | sig & \|log2FC\|>0.585 (1.5×) | sig & \|log2FC\|>1 (2×) | sig & \|log2FC\|>2 (4×) | contrast-exclusive DEGs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Final vs Baseline blood | 3,927 (17.8%) | 1,224 (5.5%) | 133 (0.6%) | 189 |
| DG vs Baseline blood | 16,474 (71.7%) | 13,408 (58.3%) | 8,610 (37.5%) | 114 |
| DG vs Final blood | 16,261 (71.1%) | 13,512 (59.1%) | 8,744 (38.3%) | 278 |

- p-value quantiles (primary): FvB q025 = 2.4e-139, median = 6.4e-20, q075 = 1.7e-02, q095 = 0.72, fraction p>0.05 = 0.191. DG vs B: q025 = 0, median = 3.7e-141, q075 = 3.1e-10, fraction p>0.05 = 0.112. DG vs F: median = 1.5e-188, q075 = 6.3e-11, fraction p>0.05 = 0.104. So observed fraction p<0.05 is 78–88% against a 5% chance expectation (15.6×–17.7× inflation) in *all three* contrasts.
- top Final-vs-Baseline genes by p are things like `Atrx` (log2FC −0.21), `Prps1l3` (+0.01), `Atp7a` (−0.07) — statistically "exact-significant", biologically null.

## 4. DEG overlaps (primary, p<0.05)
DG-vs-B ∩ DG-vs-F = 19,225 / 21,122 union → **Jaccard 0.910** (same tissue signature). FvB ∩ DG-vs-B = 16,317 (J 0.776); FvB ∩ DG-vs-F = 16,230 (J 0.766); all three = 15,520 (J 0.728) — FvB contributes almost nothing contrast-specific (189 exclusive genes vs 17,215 hits).

## 5. Plain statement on the over-powered pooled binomial (point 4 of your brief)
**Yes — the pooled exact binomial inflates the Final vs Baseline blood nominal-p hit rate massively above chance: 17,215/22,060 = 78.0% (15.6× chance, +16,112 genes over the 1,103 expected), and 44.4% even with the paired per-subject sign test.** So negligibility is *not* established by the raw p-count. The reason is structural, not biological: the pooled test treats 60 libraries as one binomial draw (median 2,668 pseudo-reads/gene) and omits between-replicate dispersion. Diagnostic: median binomial-implied SE of log2FC = 0.039 vs replicate-based SE = 0.082 → the null is ~4.4× too narrow (≈20× too narrow on variance); median between-subject SD of the paired log2 ratio is 0.45 (0.48/0.52 for the DG contrasts). A label-permutation of the paired test (9,936 vs 9,803 hits) shows the FvB hits are not subject-pairing-driven either. Consequently the interpretation is carried by (a) the consistent ranking across all six variants, (b) the 5–11× smaller |log2FC| distribution, (c) the ~11×/65× smaller DEG burden once a 2×/4-fold effect-size criterion is imposed, and (d) the fact that both DG contrasts are mutually 91% redundant and move half the transcriptome, while FvB is essentially two draws of the same tissue with subject-level scatter of ±0.45 log2 around zero (median signed log2FC exactly 0).

## 6. Deliverables / artifacts
Executed script `analysis_tissue_binomial.py` (~2 min; asserts layout 30/30/30, Index_DESeq column order, subject-pairing consistency), writing to `work/results/`: `contrast_summary.csv` (all variants, requested columns), `pvalue_quantiles.csv`, `deg_overlap.csv`, `extras.csv`, `dispersion_diagnostic.csv`, `final_vs_blood_top20.csv`, `run_log.txt`, plus per-gene p-value arrays `p_primary_*.npy` / `p_V1_*.npy` / `p_V2_paired_sign_*.npy`. Cached `work/X.npy`, `work/meta.pkl` retained; direction convention preserved (DG as numerator in both DG contrasts).

## Limitations
1. Normalized (non-integer) counts were used as pseudo-counts as fixed in the protocol; a raw-count version is not available in the capsule.
2. The primary pooled binomial has no dispersion term, so nominal p<0.05 is uninterpretable in absolute terms for all three contrasts (this is the single biggest caveat on the headline count).
3. Rounding per-arm sums to integers creates 3,342 vs 2,210 untestable genes for the blood contrast.
4. `Control_dentate_gyrus5` (Lars2 = 74% of its library) is retained in the primary run; sensitivity run shows it is not influential.
5. Responder status is pooled; the workbook's own DESeq blocks cover responder contrasts only and were not reused.
